key_takeaways: Two Australians who live at home can marry legally in Jamaica. The Ministry of Justice requires people living abroad to be on the island at least 24 hours before the marriage ceremony.

The legal key is the Minister's Marriage Licence: J$4,000 stamp duty (subject to change, per the Ministry of Justice), valid for 90 days from issue, and the Ministry encourages applying at least two weeks ahead.
The Ministry accepts original Australian documents or copies certified by a Justice of the Peace or Notary Public, and its list does not include a Certificate of No Impediment.
The register copy you sign on the day is not your proof of marriage. The certified certificate comes from the Registrar General's Department, so arrange it before you fly home.
Marrying legally in Australia first (NOIM at least one month ahead) removes the licence, the 24-hour rule and the certificate order from your Jamaica week.

faq.q: How do I get a marriage licence in Jamaica?
faq.a: Applications cannot be made online. The completed file goes to the Ministry of Justice's Customer Service Branch at 61 Constant Spring Road, Kingston 10. Stamp Duty Offices that stamp the licence form include Kingston (72 Harbour Street) and the May Pen and Montego Bay Revenue Centres.

faq.q: Do you need a blood test to get married in Jamaica?
faq.a: No. The Consulate General of Jamaica in Miami's guideline for visitors states that no blood test is required, and the Ministry of Justice's document list does not include one.

faq.q: Can same-sex couples get married in Jamaica?
faq.a: No. Section 18(2) of Jamaica's Constitution allows marriage only as the voluntary union of one man and one woman, and the Ministry of Justice issues the Minister's Marriage Licence to a man and a woman. Smartraveller also notes that same-sex relationships are illegal in Jamaica.

faq.q: Is a marriage in Jamaica legally recognised in Australia?
faq.a: Generally yes, with exceptions Smartraveller lists: either person already married, not old enough, too closely related or forced to marry. Jamaica's Ministry of Justice also puts the onus on foreign couples to confirm recognition at home before the ceremony, so settle it before you lodge the licence application.

faq.q: How long after arriving can you get married in Jamaica?
faq.a: Twenty-four hours, says the Consulate General of Jamaica in Miami, provided the licence application has already been made. The clock starts when you land, so a delayed long-haul connection pushes back the earliest possible ceremony. Leave two or more days between landing and the wedding, and confirm the timing with your Marriage Officer.
